raw_case_text:
A 30-year-old man presented with a background of end-stage renal failure secondary to birth asphyxia and with a donation after brainstem death renal transplant (baseline creatinine 290 micromol/l), maintained on sirolimus and tacrolimus. This was the patient's second transplant, the first being complicated by graft rejection, microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia and requiring graft nephrectomy in 2013. The current transplant had taken place >1 year before the current presentation, of which he had had one episode of BK viral nephropathy treated with CSs. He had been stable after this, with no significant infections. He presented with a 14-day history of feeling unwell with fevers, and a 5-day history of a cough, sore throat and difficulty breathing.
Initial oxygen saturation was 80% on room air, which improved to 100% on 35% oxygen via a venturi face mask. His blood pressure was 127/73 mmHg, heart rate 95 beats/min, temperature 38 C and respiratory rate 21 breaths/min. Chest X-ray (CXR) showed bilateral patchy consolidation, and nasopharyngeal swab (NPS) confirmed SARS-CoV-2. Blood tests revealed ferritin of 24617 microg/l, creatinine 519 micromol/l and CRP 92 mg/l.
Oxygen was titrated to keep his saturations >94%, and he was initiated on co-amoxiclav. After 2 days, with increasing oxygen requirements and progressive CXR consolidation, he was transferred to the ICU, where he was commenced on continuous positive airway pressure. The sirolimus was stopped, but he remained on tacrolimus. Ferritin at the time was 23 788 microg/l, CRP 73 mg/l and procalcitonin 17.27 mug/l (normal range <0.5 mug/l). Microscopy from blood cultures and urine cultures was negative, and CMV and EBV viraemias remained very low level. Given the increasing oxygen requirement and persistent inflammatory state, anakinra 200 mg i.v. was initiated (Table 1). A marked improvement in ferritin was seen within 2 days; CRP steadily decreased (Fig. 1), creatinine improved, and his respiratory effort stabilized. After 3 days of continuous positive airway pressure, he was weaned off and stepped down to the ward. Anakinra i.v. was stopped on day 10, when the ferritin was 4969 microg/l. He was discharged on day 12 with a creatinine of 371 micromol/l and CRP 7 mg/l and remained on tacrolimus.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 30-year-old male second-time deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient presented with a 14-day history of fevers and malaise and a 5-day history of cough, sore throat, and dyspnea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: More than 1 year after his second renal transplant (maintained on sirolimus and tacrolimus with baseline creatinine 290 umol/L), the patient presented with 14 days of fever and malaise and 5 days of cough, sore throat, and worsening shortness of breath with severe hypoxemia (SpO2 80% on room air) and hyperferritinemia (24,617 ug/L), deteriorating after 2 days to require ICU transfer and continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP).
subjective.past_medical_history: End-stage renal disease secondary to birth asphyxia status post first kidney transplant (complicated by rejection, MAHA, and graft nephrectomy in 2013) and second donation-after-brainstem-death renal transplant >1 year prior (baseline creatinine 290 umol/L; complicated by one prior episode of BK viral nephropathy treated with corticosteroids).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 14 days of fever and malaise, and 5 days of cough, sore throat, and dyspnea. Home medications: sirolimus and tacrolimus.

objective.physical_examination: Initial SpO2 80% on room air (improving to 100% on 35% Venturi mask; requiring CPAP on day 2), blood pressure 127/73 mmHg, heart rate 95 bpm, temperature 38.0 °C, and respiratory rate 21 breaths/min.
objective.routine_investigations: Nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR positive for SARS-CoV-2. Admission labs: extreme hyperferritinemia at 24,617 ug/L (23,788 ug/L on ICU admission day 2; dropping to 4,969 ug/L on day 10), acute-on-chronic allograft injury with serum creatinine 519 umol/L (baseline 290 umol/L; improving to 371 umol/L at discharge), CRP 92 mg/L (73 mg/L on day 2; 7 mg/L at discharge), and day 2 procalcitonin 17.27 ug/L (normal <0.5 ug/L). Blood and urine cultures were negative. Chest X-ray showed bilateral patchy consolidation that progressed on day 2.
objective.advanced_workup: Quantitative blood PCRs for cytomegalovirus (CMV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) showed only very low-level viremia.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with severe COVID-19 pneumonia and secondary hyperinflammatory / cytokine storm syndrome (ferritin 24,617 ug/L) with acute kidney allograft injury in a renal transplant recipient (bacterial superinfection and significant CMV or EBV reactivation ruled out). Managed in the ICU with CPAP respiratory support (weaned after 3 days), discontinuation of sirolimus while continuing tacrolimus, empiric co-amoxiclav, and a 10-day course of intravenous IL-1 receptor antagonist anakinra (200 mg IV daily), resulting in a rapid fall in ferritin (to 4,969 ug/L) and CRP (to 7 mg/L), stabilization of oxygenation, and hospital discharge on day 12 with improved graft function (creatinine 371 umol/L).
